note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md for Quran 2:261-286 (2026-11-26): 16 pictures from 32 trial pictures. Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper 60% of the frame, clear of the word box. The Prophet Muhammad is never shown in any way, nor anyone standing in for him; God and the angels are not pictured; no religious symbols of any tradition; nothing violent. Tried and not chosen: A single grain of wheat in a palm and beside it one huge stalk heavy with ears. A man leaves a gift basket at a gate and turns away down the lane. A rainstorm washes the soil off a rooftop garden leaving bare concrete. A hillside garden terrace overflowing with fruit and vines after rain. A whirlwind of fire spins over a palm grove at dusk, no one in sight. A man gives away a torn shoe and keeps a new pair. A hooded figure puts a folded note of money into a donation box on a dark street corner. An old woman sits with a small basket of lemons and her head held high at a market corner. A thick vine of coins winds around a small house and tightens. A man hands a neighbor a glass of water on the porch of a small house on a hot afternoon. Two men shake hands over a signed paper with a witness watching. A neighbor returns a lent lamp wrapped in cloth to its owner without a scratch. A wide lit window with its curtains drawn back to show the whole room to the dark street. A runner at the start hears a whistle and bursts forward at once. A farmer loads a donkey with a fitting load and no more, and strokes its neck. A pair of open hands are lifted to the first rain after a long drought.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the part into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: What is spent in God's way is like a grain that grew seven ears with a hundred grains in each; do not follow charity with reminders or hurt, like a smooth rock with a little soil that a downpour leaves bare.
ideas: One stalk of wheat with seven heavy ears rising from one seed in golden light
A woman quietly leaves a bag of groceries on a neighbor's doorstep and walks away unseen
A smooth rock slab with a thin layer of soil being stripped bare by a downpour

sections.meaning: Those who spend seeking to please God are like a garden on high ground that gives its produce twice over after a downpour; would any of you love a garden with rivers beneath it, in old age with weak children, to see a fiery whirlwind burn it?
ideas: A hilltop orchard heavy with fruit in light rain and mist
An old man with two small children before a burned and blackened orchard
A whirlwind of fire spinning over a palm grove at dusk

sections.meaning: Spend from the good things and do not aim to give the bad of it, which you would not take yourselves unless you shut your eyes to it; Satan promises poverty, God promises forgiveness and bounty.
ideas: A woman holds out a bruised rotten apple to a beggar while keeping a fresh one for herself
A man gives away a torn shoe and keeps the new pair

sections.meaning: Charity disclosed is fine, but hidden and given to the poor is better; it is for the poor who are held back and do not ask people insistently; an ignorant person supposes them rich because of their restraint.
ideas: An envelope slid under a door at night by an unseen hand
A man in a patched but immaculate coat stands with quiet dignity at the edge of a busy street not asking
An old woman sells a few lemons with her head high

sections.meaning: Those who eat up interest are not able to stand; God wipes out interest and makes charity grow; if there is someone in difficulty, time is to be given until ease.
ideas: A tiny snowball grown huge rolls down a hill toward a small house
A vine of coins strangling a small house
Two men leaning on a fence watching a young crop grow in a poor field, one's hand on the other's shoulder

sections.meaning: When you contract a debt, write it down, with a scribe and witnesses; what was entrusted must be handed back; do not conceal testimony; what is within yourselves, disclosed or hidden, God will reckon.
ideas: A scribe's hand writes a ledger line while two men sign and two witnesses stand by
A man hands back a sealed bag of coins to its owner with the seal unbroken
A glass house lit at night with every room visible to the dark field around it

sections.meaning: The messenger and the believers say 'we hear and we obey'; God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity; they ask not to be loaded with a weight they cannot bear, and to be pardoned, forgiven and shown mercy.
ideas: A man hears a distant bell and his feet are already walking toward it
A father carries a big pack and his small child a tiny pack on the same path
A child hugged by a parent after being forgiven, in morning light

scenes.principle: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is like that of a grain that grew seven ears, with a hundred grains in every ear. And God multiplies for whomever he wills, and God is vast, knowing.
scenes.shows: One stalk of wheat with seven heavy ears, each full of grain, rises from one seed in a golden field.
scenes.prompt: One single tall stalk of wheat with seven heavy full ears branching from it, each heavy with a hundred grains, rising in a golden field at golden hour, in close sharp focus with the field softly behind. The stalk and its ears are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: Those who spend their wealth in the way of God, and then do not follow what they have spent with reminders of it or with hurt, they have their reward with their Lord, and there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve.
scenes.shows: A woman quietly sets a bag of groceries on a neighbor's doorstep and walks away without being seen.
scenes.prompt: A woman in plain clothes quietly sets a full bag of groceries on a neighbor's front doorstep at dusk and walks away on tiptoe without looking back, the closed door unaware, soft light. The woman and the bag are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: You who believe, do not make your charity worthless with reminders of it and with hurt, like the one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in God and the Last Day.
scenes.shows: A smooth rock slab with a thin layer of soil is stripped bare by a downpour, the soil running off in streams.
scenes.prompt: A smooth gray rock slab on a hillside with a thin layer of soil on top being washed away by a heavy downpour, muddy streams running off and the smooth bare rock showing through, no plants left. The rock and the streams are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking to please God and to make themselves firm is like that of a garden on high ground: a downpour struck it, so it gave its produce twice over, and if no downpour strikes it, then light ...
scenes.shows: A hilltop orchard heavy with fruit stands in soft rain and mist after a downpour.
scenes.prompt: A green orchard on a hilltop heavy with ripe fruit on every branch in soft rain and mist after a downpour, the leaves glistening, fruit gleaming, golden light breaking through. The orchard is in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.from: Would any of you love to have a garden
scenes.principle: Would any of you love to have a garden of date palms and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it, where he has fruits of every kind, and old age has struck him, and he has weak children, and then a whirlwind with fire in it strikes it ...
scenes.shows: An old man with two small children stands before his orchard of palms burned black, smoke still rising.
scenes.prompt: An old man in plain clothes stands with two small children beside him before his orchard of date palms and grapevines burned black, smoke still rising from the ashes, gray light, seen from behind. The old man, the children and the burned trees are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: You who believe, spend from the good things you have earned and from what we have brought out of the earth for you. And do not aim for the bad of it to spend, when you would not take it yourselves unless you shut your eyes to it.
scenes.shows: A woman holds out a bruised rotten apple to a beggar while a fresh red apple is in her other hand.
scenes.prompt: A woman in plain clothes holds out a bruised rotten apple to a poor man with an open hand, while in her other hand she keeps a fresh red apple for herself, bright light. The woman, the poor man and both apples are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: If you disclose charity, it is a fine thing. But if you hide it and give it to the poor, that is better for you, and he will remove some of your evil deeds from you. And God is aware of what you do.
scenes.shows: An unseen hand slides an envelope under a door at night.
scenes.prompt: Close on a plain front door at night and a hand just letting go of an envelope sliding it under the door, the hand pulling away into the dark, a warm light from inside the house. The door and the envelope are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: It is for the poor who are held back in the way of God and cannot travel in the land. An ignorant person supposes them rich because of their restraint. You recognize them by their mark. They do not ask people insistently.
scenes.shows: A man in a patched but immaculate coat stands with quiet dignity at the edge of a busy street, not asking for anything.
scenes.prompt: A man in a patched but immaculately clean coat stands with quiet dignity at the edge of a busy street, hands at his sides, head up, not asking for anything, passersby walking past not noticing him. The man is in the upper two thirds of the picture. No church, no bell tower, no steeple and no tower of any kind anywhere in the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: Those who eat up interest do not stand except as one stands whom Satan beats down by his touch. That is because they said, "Selling is only like interest." But God has permitted selling and forbidden interest.
scenes.shows: A tiny snowball has grown huge as it rolls down a mountainside toward a small house in the valley.
scenes.prompt: A giant snowball grown enormous rolling down a snowy mountainside toward a small house in the valley below, a trail of rolling marks behind it, bright cold light. The snowball and the house are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: And if there is someone in difficulty, then time is to be given until ease. And to give charity is better for you, if you know.
scenes.shows: Two men lean on a fence watching a young crop grow, one resting a hand on the other's shoulder.
scenes.prompt: Two men in plain work clothes lean on a fence together looking at a poor field of young green shoots just coming up, one patting the other kindly on the shoulder, calm light. The two men and the shoots are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: You who believe, when you contract a debt with one another for a named term, write it down. And let a scribe write it down between you justly. And let no scribe refuse to write as God has taught him.
scenes.shows: A scribe's hand writes a line in a ledger while two men sign and two witnesses stand by.
scenes.prompt: Close on a plain table: a scribe's hand writing a line in a big ledger book, with no legible words, two men's hands holding pens to sign and two witnesses standing behind them, warm window light. The ledger and the hands are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then security taken in hand. But if one of you trusts another, let the one who is trusted hand back what he was trusted with, and let him be mindful of God, his Lord.
scenes.shows: A man hands a sealed bag of coins back to its owner at a doorway with the seal unbroken.
scenes.prompt: A man in plain clothes hands a sealed leather bag of coins back to its owner at a doorway with the wax seal unbroken, both looking each other in the eye, morning light. The two men and the bag are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: To God belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. And if you disclose what is within yourselves or hide it, God will reckon with you for it. Then he forgives whomever he wills and punishes whomever he wills.
scenes.shows: A house of glass is lit at night with every room visible to the dark field around it, a lone person sitting in one room.
scenes.prompt: A house made entirely of glass lit warmly at night in a dark field so that every room is visible, a lone person in plain clothes sitting with head bowed in one room, nothing hidden. The glass house is in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: The messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers.
scenes.shows: A man hears a distant bell and turns, his feet already walking toward it.
scenes.prompt: A man in plain clothes stands on a village path cupping one hand to his ear toward a distant clear bell sound and his whole body and feet already turned and walking toward the sound, the path leading on to a bright horizon. The man is in the upper two thirds of the picture. No church, no bell tower, no steeple and no tower of any kind anywhere in the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it earned, and against it is what it earned. "Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make a mistake.
scenes.shows: A father carries a big pack and his small child a tiny pack on the same path, each carrying what he can.
scenes.prompt: A father with a big pack and his small child with a tiny pack walk the same mountain path together in clear morning light, each carrying what he can bear, seen from behind. The father and the child are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.from: And pardon us, and forgive us
scenes.principle: God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it earned, and against it is what it earned. "Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make a mistake.
scenes.shows: A child is hugged by a parent after being forgiven, in warm morning light.
scenes.prompt: A child in plain clothes with a tear-streaked face is hugged tightly by a parent kneeling in a doorway in warm morning light, forgiven, relief on both faces. The two are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.
